claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa near 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has significant room-temperature ductility.
The proposed intervention replaces 10–20% of the Mo and/or Ta content in HfMoTaTiZr with V or Cr.
Partial substitution of Mo and/or Ta by V or Cr will reduce alloy density by approximately 5–10%.
The V- or Cr-substituted alloy will retain near-baseline mechanical performance from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The substituted alloy will remain a stable single-phase or predominantly single-phase BCC solid solution.
Maintaining a predominantly BCC solid solution will preserve the alloy's beneficial strengthening mechanisms.
V or Cr substitution lowers average atomic mass and therefore lowers the alloy density.
V or Cr can preserve solid-solution strengthening and high-temperature stability because refractory elements have similar atomic sizes and bonding characteristics.
The substituted alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength of at least 1500 MPa.
The substituted alloy will have a yield strength of at least 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The substituted alloy will retain at least 10% room-temperature ductility.
Substitution above 20% of the Mo/Ta content may produce brittle intermetallic phases.
Substitution above 20% may cause decomposition of the single-phase BCC matrix and undermine high-temperature performance.
Unanticipated compounds or precipitates may form and alter strength and ductility.
Mechanical performance is to be tested from 22 °C to 1000 °C at a constant engineering strain rate under ambient atmosphere.
The hypothesis is rejected if density falls by less than 5% or if room-temperature strength, 1000 °C strength, or ductility decreases by more than 10% relative to the baseline.
